All green. Writing it up and packaging v3.23.

The check is done. The live app is sound, and the one real weakness it turned up is fixed in v3.23, attached here as four files. (Your laptop still isn’t reachable from this chat, so I couldn’t put them in the Desktop folder myself.)

What I ran, on the exact files from GitHub, served the way GitHub serves them

  • All twelve existing suites: passed. Install, offline, weak signal, roster, meal order, recipe sharing, nine screen sizes, text size, accessibility, data integrity and the shopping list.
  • New: a tap-only walkthrough with no shortcuts, from an empty app to a shared plan: counters, meals, picking recipes by tapping, building the list, ticking rows, sharing, roster names, adding a recipe through the form, reload, undo. All passed.
  • New: upgrade from v3.21 with a saved plan, roster swaps and a phone recipe. Everything carried over, and the old cache was cleaned out.
  • New: stress. 30 recipes, 30 names on a 14-day roster, 40 rapid taps, repeated tab switching. No errors; the menu draws in 48 ms and the list in 110 ms.
  • New: keyboard-only use on a laptop. Counters, chips and tabs all work.
  • New: an independent audit of the MyPlate tagging by a second agent that hadn’t seen my work. This is where the findings were.

What was wrong

  • Eggs counted double, so brownies and cakes showed up as Protein.
  • Ingredients were judged one at a time, so a scramble’s peppers plus onion didn’t add up to Vegetables.
  • Small amounts counted: a smear of pizza sauce passed as a vegetable, and a spoon of milk powder made cocoa count as Dairy.
  • Desserts counted toward the menu, so S’mores could supply the Grains.
  • The wording called the check “the answer” to First Class 2a. A Scoutmaster would object, since the Scout is meant to give that answer, and 2a also asks about the needs of the activity.
  • Two small ones: the zip code only saved when you tapped a store button, and typing names into a very long roster lagged.

v3.23 fixes all of those. Across all 148 recipes, 21 changed grouping, all in the direction the audit asked for. The dessert row is now greyed and marked “not counted”, and the text tells Scouts to use the check against their own answer.

To publish: save the four files into Desktop\Troop-Mess-upload with those exact names (index.html should be about 282 KB), upload them to GitHub, and tell me. I’ll confirm the live copy matches.
